items.meta_title: Cloak Mode: Undetectable VPN Traffic | VpnHood!
items.meta_description: Cloak Mode disguises VPN traffic as ordinary web traffic, so deep packet inspection (DPI) has no signature to match. Available in VpnHood!
items.title: Cloak Mode
items.lead: Overcomes VPN blocks by disguising your VPN traffic as regular web traffic, making it resistant to deep packet inspection (DPI).
items.shot_alt: The Cloak Mode screen in the VpnHood! app
items.diagram_desc: Without Cloak Mode, your device sends packets through one long tunnel. A network filter cannot see inside it, but its bumpy shape gives it away, and the filter can drop it. With Cloak Mode, each connection is a request of its own, in a smooth tunnel that looks like web browsing to the filter.
items.diagram_off_result: Its shape can give it away
items.diagram_caption: Cloak Mode changes what a filter sees
items.how_desc: Most VPN traffic has a shape that a network filter can recognize and drop. Cloak Mode makes it look like ordinary web traffic instead, leaving little for a filter to match. It hides what the traffic is, not where it goes.
items.when_desc: Turn it on when a network is actively fighting VPNs: a school or office firewall, hotel and airport Wi-Fi that blocks tunnels, or a national filter. On a home connection that is not blocking anything, you do not need it.
items.cost_desc: Cloaked traffic carries more overhead than a direct tunnel, so it can be a little slower and use slightly more battery. That is the trade: raw speed when nothing is in your way, a connection that still works when something is.
items.step1_desc: You will find it on the app's home screen.
items.step2_desc: It is the first switch on the Protocols screen.
items.step3_desc: Back on the home screen, Cloak appears beside Protocol.
